utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. In practice, it should have?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you -- before I show you this next document -- rather, let me call it up, but -- it's going to be P554. But with respect to the document that's on the screen now, that should have gone to the commander of the Main Staff as an order from the Supreme Commander?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is addressed to the Main Staff, then it should have reached it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you P554B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is under seal and should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I am showing you is an intercept [microphone not activated] dated 17 July at 2055 hours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At 17 July at 2055 hours. And it concerns an exchange between someone named -- we are going to have to go to the next page in the B/C/S, please. It's the last intercept here, 2055. Thank you. It concerns a conversation between someone named Trivic and someone named Jankovic, Colonel Jankovic. First of all, did you know a Colonel Jankovic in the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember anybody by that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember anybody by the name of Radoslav Jankovic, Colonel Radoslav Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has heard evidence that Colonel Radoslav Jankovic was an intelligence officer in the intelligence administration of the security and intelligence sector of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some people in that sector with whom I didn't have contact. I do not remember a Colonel Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, this is a conversation between Colonel Jankovic and a person named Trivic, and you can read it. It says: "Give me Colonel Jankovic. "Just a second." And then he gets on the line and says: "I am listening." And Trivic says: "Well, Jankovic. "Listen here. Miletic said that you should write what you want to do and send it urgently by code up to Tolimir. I am in no position to write," Jankovic says. And Trivic says: "Listen to what I am telling you." And then says -- Jankovic says: "All right." And Trivic says: "And the commander will decide with Tolimir and send you a reply." I want to show you another document which is P2168.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, just to let you know, you have approximately ten minutes left for your cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is document as you can see which is directed to -- this is a document which you can see which is directed to the security and intelligence department of the -- rather, sector of the Main Staff. You can see at the bottom of the -- this particular document it indicates the name of Momir Nikolic. We will have to go to page 3 in the -- I think it's 3 in the B/C/S. And then we have a corresponding translation for that. And we can see the handwritten version of this document. And at the bottom, on the next page - we will have to go to the next page, please - you see the initials "RJ." And the Trial Chamber has heard evidence that that RJ is Radoslav Jankovic. In this document you can see that it's dated 18 July. And I want to draw your attention to item number 3 in this document which says that: "The Medecins Sans Frontieres convoy, which arrived on 18 July 1995, at 1400 hours, at the Ljubovija crossing, for transportation of their staff from the UNPROFOR base in Potocari was sent back for procedural reasons (apparently they should have entered via Zvornik)." If you go further down, you will see it says: "Will you please tell me what stand to take in terms of authorisation for evacuation of the International organisation, Medicins Sans Frontiers, in fact, how to deal with the so-called local staff." Did you get information about this particular request?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen or heard of this request before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It makes sense, would it not, that Colonel Jankovic would have sent this request for instruction to General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It makes sense that this issue would have been brought to the attention of Colonel Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not even Colonel Djurdjic had to be acquainted with all details of the activities of the security organs in the field. It was not usual practice to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me show you 65 ter 383 -- P. I'm sorry, P383. 383B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This should not be broadcast because it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We will have to go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You can see that this one is dated 19 July, and we will go to the intercept at 1432 hours. This is an intercept, as you can see, between Jankovic and Colonel Djurdjic. We can go through it briefly. It says: "Djurdjic: Colonel Djurdjic speaking." That's about the fourth line down. And then it talks about: "Djurdjic: The boss has ordered that they be halted." Jankovic says: "Yes. "Djurdjic: This is what he wrote. "Jankovic: Yes. "Djurdjic: Kristina Smit [phoen], the nurse, can go. "Djurdjic: Daniel O'Brian [phoen]. "Djurdjic: The physician." If we go to the next page in the English. And they discuss women and children. And then Jankovic says: "So, they have permission from the Koljevic government?" And Djurdjic says: "Yes. "That they can all go, they have a list," Jankovic says. "Djurdjic: Yes, I know ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We will have to go to the next page: "Yes, I know ... can I see the names" -- "I can see the names," rather. And he starts naming individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We will have to go to the next page in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And he names Abdulah Kurtovic, Ibrahim Ibrahimovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should go back one page in English. There you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you can see the names there: Muhidin Husic, Muhamed Hasic, Masic, Sahin Talovic, Hajrudin Kurtic, Omer Talovic. And if we continue down, you will see that Djurdjic says: "All right, they have the permission, but you know that the procedure you, too, took part in ..." Jankovic says: "Great, if that's your position, it's good." Djurdjic says: "The procedure is such, God damn it, that it should be checked whether those who" -- "whether those who ... are they able-bodied or older than 60." And ask Jankovic -- Jankovic says: "They are able-bodied." And he confirms it. And so Djurdjic says: "So that's the procedure. And you know [sic] what you left behind in Bratunac the other day." This conversation, the Trial Chamber has received evidence of, and I will show you, concerns the so-called local staff of the MSF. And in particular, Djurdjic is referring to a procedure related to whether or not these individuals are able-bodied or older than 60. Can you tell me what information you had, if any, about the circumstances of the evacuation of these so-called local workers for MSF in your unit or sector?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have never seen this before. I don't know the person in question. The other one, I mean. Nor did I have any information from Colonel Djurdjic about any talks he was involved in, nor was it present when this took place. I haven't the faintest idea about this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can continue down. It says: "Let the elderly go, and tonight, when Toso arrives, you and him must make sure you consult some more ..." Who is Toso, Mr. Kralj?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot identify Toso here. I didn't contact anybody in that area who was called Toso.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know anybody by the name of Toso? Did you at that time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such name on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know anybody by that nickname?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A nickname is something else. General Tolimir may have been called Toso by some people, but that wouldn't be anything I know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 7583 in e-court, please. And it's transcript page 29289.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What about the remaining time for your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have one other document that I would like to show Mr. Kralj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that Mr. Tolimir has the chance to re-examine the witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. President. I don't know if Mr. Gajic or Mr. Tolimir is in a position to let us know. That would be helpful to me, anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, do you have any idea how much time you will need for your re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I'll have about five questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then you should bear that in mind, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I would like to refer you to, Mr. Kralj, is beginning at page -- line 6 of this page. You were asked this question by General Miletic's lawyer with respect to a document. It was a convoy document that was put to you. And it reads: "Do you recognise the initials underneath the handwritten comment that we see at the very top of the page?" And you say: "This is General Mladic's initial." Then she asks you: "Something is handwritten, and we see -- and then the rest is illegible. Who is Toso?" And your answer was: "General Tolimir." You know Toso to be General Tolimir. That's correct, isn't it, Mr. Kralj?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that General Mladic called General Tolimir Toso, and that is what I confirmed. However, talking about the document we have just seen, I don't know if Colonel Djurdjic means General Tolimir. General Mladic did call the general Toso sometimes; however, those with a lower rank than his did not call him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me show you P1214. This is a Main Staff document. It's dated 17 March 1995. And it says: "Directive for upcoming operations." It says: "Enclosed with this document we are sending you the directive for further operations number 7." And you can see there General Milovanovic's name. First of all, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should go back to the first page in English, and there must be a corresponding page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The corresponding page in B/C/S, for some reason, is at the end of document. So if we go to the last page in the B/C/S, we will find the corresponding page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, there it is. Now, please, repeat your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no opportunity to see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me show you the first page of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We will have to go to the second page in both.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise it now?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the upper right-hand corner, there is the confidentiality indication. Lower levels, and especially mine, were not allowed to see documents qualified or classified as state secret. No, I haven't seen any document of this type.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You can see the top of this document is dated 8 March 1995. And let me just take you to -- it should be page 11 in the English and -- just bear with me one moment. It should be page 8, I think, in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The preceding page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, you will see it says, "Drina Corps." It says: "Enemy break-throughs along selected operative-tactical lines should be prevented by extremely persistent and active defence in co-operation with part of the forces of the SRK on the north-west part of the war front and around the enclaves. As many enemy forces as possible should be tied down by diversionary and active combat operations on the north-west part of the front using operational and tactical camouflage measures, while in the direction of the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves complete physical separation of Srebrenica and Zepa should be carried out as soon as possible, preventing even communications between individuals in the two enclaves." And then it says: "By planned and well-thought-out combat operations create an unbearable situation of total insecurity with no hope of further survival or life for the inhabitants of Srebrenica and Zepa." Have you seen that before?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you heard of it before?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, nobody familiarised me with the military political situation or these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to take you to the next-to-last page in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we'll have to go to the next-to-last page in the English, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here, I want to direct you to what is the third paragraph from the bottom in the English. It talks about moral and psychological support in item 6.1. But in that -- under that topic, it says: "The relevant state and military organs responsible for work with UNPROFOR and humanitarian organisations shall, through the planned and unobtrusively restrictive issuing of permits, reduce and limit the logistics support of UNPROFOR to the enclaves and the supply of material resources to the Muslim population, making them dependent on our good will while at the same time avoiding condemnation by the international community and international public opinion." Have you heard that before?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am not familiar with this document. It is possible that Colonel Milos had some information, but he didn't relay it to me because of this high confidentiality classification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The specific reference to UNPROFOR and the supply of aid to the Muslim population and humanitarian organisations referred to in this passage is something that falls within Colonel Djurdjic's competence; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is true. I believe that the colonel was abreast of that, but I didn't know anything. He didn't relay such information to me because such secrets are only passed on to other persons with the obligation on the latter to sign for this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would you follow a directive like this if you received it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I said last time, too, that a question of the type, "what would you have done if," is not appropriate. I would certainly have opted for the lesser evil, but there is the rule of subordination in the army. That doesn't necessarily mean that I would have been part of that chain, too. Please don't make me comment on things that are inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What you said, Mr. Kralj - and this was in your Popovic testimony - at transcript page 29371, starting at line 23 - this is 65 ter 7583 - through page 29372, line 18, was as follows, "My question to you was" -- "Maybe there was a translation error, but my question was: You wouldn't follow that directive, would you?" And your answer was: "I would warn the ones who would be issuing such a directive of the consequences. In our army, orders were not executed blindly. If something was unclear, there was the option of asking for additional explanations." What would you warn someone issuing such a directive of? What consequences were you referring to in your answer?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, everything you read out is correct. As part of my military education, I also attended a post-war course in international laws of war, which was a bi-weekly course organised by the ICRC in Italy. I learned many things there as to what things one may be held responsible for during wartime. And I also know that if a superior is making a mistake in the way a decision was made, a subordinate officer should warn him. And I'm saying this because I am trying to say that if my superior decided something, I may not be held accountable.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kralj.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions. And I appreciate your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are over the time for the break. We need our second break now. It will be a little bit shorter and we should resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, before you get the floor, let me put one small question to the witness. Mr. Kralj, you travelled here with a passport. When did you request to get a passport to your -- from your Serbian authorities? Approximately. It's not necessary to give us an exact date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After a conversation I had with counsel. He asked me if I had a passport. I told him I did. It was still valid but it was not the new BiH passport. He instructed me to get a new passport then, and the RS authorities, as part of regular procedure, issued my passport on the 12th of December, 2011.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Says the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I submitted a request a few weeks before that. The 12th of December, 2011.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kralj, I take it that you had a conversation with the team member of Mr. Tolimir in December or even earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the passport was issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I put this question to you because at the beginning of the cross-examination by Mr. Vanderpuye, you said you were contacted first by Mr. Gajic some 20 days ago. That would be at the beginning of January. But now, I think, you have corrected that and you were contacted first already last year; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, now you may commence your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kralj, can you tell us where you were in July 1995 at the time of events in Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, sir, during the events in Srebrenica, I was in Banja Luka attending a burial of my mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In April and May 1995, did it happen that some convoys were approved by the Main Staff following notifications without the convoys actually being realised across RS territory?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such announced convoys. They were approved but did not go through at the time. It was never explained why.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kralj, as regards observer rotations in the demilitarised zone, were they taking place individually and on a daily basis or according to shifts and in keeping with the announced dates for observer rotations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rotations were supposed to take place periodically. The time-period in question should have been several days apart, but it also happened that certain individuals were replaced even after shorter periods of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 60 of today's transcript, lines 1 through 10, Mr. Vanderpuye asked you what caution you would issue to your supervisors. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see the document again, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the Court Usher, you will see it in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I will remind you he was reading from a directive of the Supreme Commander and a decision of the corps commander. And then he put the question. My question is this: Could you caution or warn the Supreme Commander and the corps commanders, and did you know whether you were shown documents in the Main Staff or whether there were such documents produced in the Main Staff such as the one shown to you by Mr. Vanderpuye before he put his question?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, sir, I am not familiar with anything contained in such documents. My department or me, personally, could not suggest anything that we were not familiar with. The question was a general one to the effect that, if I received an order as an officer, if I could comment before implementing the order. So it didn't pertain to the Main Staff in general. My explanation relied on the system of subordination. I was a lieutenant-colonel. If Djurdjic ordered me to do something, I could tell him what I thought about what he had ordered. That's what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kralj. Can you tell us whether you were shown documents of the Main Staff when the question was put to you by Mr. Vanderpuye? Was it a Main Staff document or were these documents sent to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the signature block, I could see the signature of the president of the republic which means that the Main Staff received it from him, and the president was at a different location.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kralj. Thank you for the answers you provided to us and the Prosecution. Thank you for your testimony, and thank you for sharing your point of view with the Chamber about the issues at the time. I have no more questions for you. I would like to thank you and wish you a safe journey and may God bless you with a long life.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has no further questions of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. Mr. Kralj, you will be pleased to hear that this concludes your examination here in the Tribunal. Thank you very much that you were able to come here and provide us with your knowledge and expertise. Now you are free to return to your normal activities. Thank you very much, again, and goodbye. We adjourn for the day, and we will resume on Monday in this courtroom at 2.15 in the afternoon. One moment, please. My colleague reminded me that there was a request that Mr. Kralj would have the opportunity to visit Mr. Tolimir in the Detention Unit. Now he is released. He is a free man. If there are -- he will better know than we do, because the Chamber is not involved in these procedures, how that could be arranged that the witness could visit, not in his capacity as a witness but as a free man to come to the Detention Unit and carry out a visit. Mr. Gajic, you may be in a position to assist Mr. Kralj in that respect. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. Tolimir was notified that the visit was approved, but we still don't know the fate of Mr. Kralj's request. We were told that we would be informed once Mr. Kralj's testimony was over. So, for the time being, in other words, we are unable to tell you anything more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: As everybody will be aware, the Registry is the relevant institution to deal with these matters and to decide on such a request, not the Chamber, but I talked to the Court Officer and he will forward this request immediately to OLAD so that a decision can be made. And I think, Mr. Kralj, after we have left the courtroom, you may discuss it and get further information by the Registrar here in the courtroom. Thank you very much. We resume on Monday and now we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 30th day of January, 2012, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.17 p.m.,
